key_insight: OpenBrain pairs generated whole-brain MRI labels with auditable case records, helping researchers assess which labels are reliable enough to reuse. The release covers 35,838 provenance-verified T1-weighted MRI cases from 607 OpenNeuro datasets.
problem_solved: Large-scale generated MRI label releases often lack the evidence needed to judge individual cases, making label reuse and quality assessment difficult.
method: Assemble 35,838 provenance-verified T1-weighted MRI cases from 607 OpenNeuro source datasets.
Organize the release around auditable case records rather than standalone segmentation files.
Link each case to a primary parcellation and two committee parcellations within a confidence-aware release.
impact: OpenBrain provides a more traceable resource for practitioners reusing generated brain labels in AI/ML workflows. Its case-level organization supports scrutiny of label reliability rather than treating every generated segmentation as equally trustworthy.
visual_elements: Scale graphic highlighting 35,838 MRI cases across 607 source datasets.

paper_title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation
paper_authors: Qizhen Lan, Yu-Chun Hsu, Yuxiang Wei, Lijing Zhu, Zenan Sun
